result.scientific_strategy:
## c92ccfe2-1135-4ec4-bc5a-eded729fc461 / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 196 successes out of 200 official episodes on the unchanged full-range reach-and-hold task. The strongest saved policy, checkpoint-100352 (working and best-known), succeeds on 1945/2000 = 97.25% of two disjoint 1000-episode full-range panels (97.2% seed 6000, 97.3% seed 8000), with 99.5% on the reused seed-5000 selection panel and 98.0% on the reused task-reference panel. Later working controls measured 98.6% and 97.0% on seeds 11000 and 12000, so the larger development evidence remains below the objective. The deficit is in-distribution and angularly localized rather than radial: the lower-left sector carries nearly all failures, including 72.9% in [-150,-120) and 96.6% in [-180,-150). Across the two large baseline panels, 28 of 55 failures never entered tolerance and 27 entered but held fewer than 50 of the required 100 steps. A fresh unchanged run instead reached only 15.1% and 17.4% at its measured checkpoints, so the working policy is not a typical fresh outcome under the observed process.

**Lessons and limits:** The 14-20 cm training annulus was not the binding gap: near targets (6-14 cm) generalize at about 97.6%, no worse than the trained bands. Extended training of the same recipe gave no measured gain: checkpoint-100352 beats checkpoint-120832 on a shared 1000-episode panel (97.2% versus 96.2%) and every paired comparison (12-1 over 1200 episodes); checkpoints 115712 and 105472 also remain behind. Training proxies plateaued while measured failures stayed angularly structured, and proxy peaks for both challengers did not predict task success. The 50% lower-left curriculum and full hold-progress forfeiture interventions did not produce durable gains. The 11-value observation includes both analytic IK branches, but code inspection shows that one branch can violate the +/-170 degree joint limits in the residual sector while the other remains feasible; this is a plausible mechanism, not measured causal evidence. Reward-only changes preserve the existing policy I/O and action semantics, whereas representation changes would require a new inference contract and a fresh learning process. The large panels are development evidence with selection context, the task-reference panel is reused, and the angular decomposition is descriptive. Experiment 2 is invalid and unmeasured; its attempted curriculum change is neither a positive nor negative result.

**Open questions:** It remains uncertain whether the lower-left never-enter failures are primarily optimization errors, confusion between analytic IK branches, or the joint-limit geometry exposed by those branches. It also remains uncertain whether hold-boundary oscillation is stable across recipes, and how much fresh-initialization variance the single failed replication represents. These uncertainties affect different campaign decisions: choosing between a semantically compatible training intervention, a new representation contract, or further process-variance study. They are recorded for reassessment and do not prescribe an action.
